I loved bonerasier minions and I really enjoyed the first demo/alpha that was released for this game. However, I am very disappointed with the direction this game went in. Lots of systems exist in this game that are awkward or just unfun. Edit 1: I wasn't sure if this was confirmed until now, but apparently there is a soft cap on the amount of cogs you can get each level. Not only does this mean you HAVE to get cog items and enemy spawners just to reach nearly the same amount of cogs every level, but you get no fulfilling progress on your econ throughout the game. Feels like another underbaked, deeply unsatisfying mechanic. - Most of the characters are either completely unfun (the first 5 characters are just copy and pasted versions of each other that promote you limiting your build as much as possible) or outright bad (cog gobbler is beyond bad and wretch, blacksmith, and merchant are all also bad) - Each difficulty limits what weapons and elements you can use. Why is this an issue? Well, if you start with a weapon that isn't argon at the first difficulty of either campaign or endless (and you can start with any noncombination weapon in the game) you cannot upgrade that weapon AT ALL for the rest of the run. Not to mention, if you're playing one of the 5 copy and pasted characters who's a higher tier than the difficulty, you're flat out useless - The element system is both boring, restricting, and very weird. All weapons have an element that they get increased stats with the more of said element you have. You can also get body stats from elements too (which are very important), but you have to hope you fish for an item that lets you get body stats from these elements in the first place. Not only is juggling different elements usually not worth it, but its entirely luck dependent on if you get the elements you want in the shop. Not to mention a solid portion of the elemental upgrades (like the temporary stat buffs or generators apart from endless) are useless or not worth the cogs. Apart from that, the elements do nothing on their own and have no flare that makes each element unique apart from them being associated with different stages and weapons. If you shuffled the elements around for each weapon, it would make zero difference in the game. - Your shop options can be taken up with locked items! This means that you can theoretically have only 1 choice in the shop, or none at all! - Weapon traits are very spammy and promote very little strategy. Each weapon has a trait that makes it unique and can be applied to other weapons to combine effects (such as one weapon having explosive projectiles and another having homing shots). However, you have very little agency when it comes to acquiring these traits. If you want your weapons to have multiple traits, you have to buy them from a shop which applies the weapon traits to ALL of your weapons, even ones that don't have a use for certain traits. This means that you can't build each individual weapon you have to a certain style, its either all or nothing. Also, because having a weapon lets you have that perk for free in the shop (it might also have a higher chance to appear too, not sure?) this promotes you buying and selling weapons for as many perks as you can so you can just add as much text as possible to weapons, removing every inch of strategy for weapon choice. In the first alpha, weapon traits were passed on with a weapon combination system, where you could merge weapons together to get increased stats and a combo of traits. This system was FAR superior to the one we have now (apart from promoting you to only having 1 super weapon instead of multiple, I still believe the combination system with tweaks and limitations would be better than the one we have now) - Speaking of weapon traits, correct me if I'm wrong but I'm pretty sure you just can't get them in endless mode at all apart from the default ones weapons come with - Environments are more or less the same between each stage, apart from color background differences and new map nodes. Most enemies are recolored or re-skinned versions of each other with little variation in how you handle them, especially as you progress in difficulties - This is super nitpicky, but the "Card game" the dev likes to add to their games in this version isn't nearly as fun as Bonerasier's game, but that might just be a me thing. It also seems much more difficult to win - If anything I said here is subject to taste, the one thing I can say for certain is that the "final boss" of each difficulty is the least inspired and most boring boss I think I have ever faced in video gaming history. Each boss is just a recolored version of this idle, base thing that shoots at you, with each difficulty replacing an attack for a new one. Little to no variation at all I really hope a lot of these issues gets improved, as the game has a really cool visual style and great soundtrack. I know the dev makes amazing stuff but this game just has not landed for me yet. It's a shame too, the unfinished campaign mode looks like it would be seriously fun, but its not out yet.

Good game play but hard to look at. I genuinely enjoy the game play & decision making but sadly the game is not playable for me right now. The game frequently uses "glitchy" transition animations that give me headaches after a few rounds. There are also a few menus that are kind of hard to read. The combat stages themselves are fine.
画风和前作一样，但是目前切换界面时画面会像噪点一样，看着不舒服。ea阶段东西不多，没中文，可以期待一手。

Updated 11/27/24: I voted for this for my "Sit Back and Relax Award" for Stam Awards. It is incredibly zen despite the fact it is "faster" and goes in 69+ second rounds. There's an enjoyable rhythm between the stages, the hacking, the shopping...this game is oft part of my nightly ritual. Really funky. The campaign mode, whose demo is out, is very promising. The performance on my craptop that stutters playing the 1990s CRPG Lands of Lore has improved to be a solid 60fps even when there's loads of crap onscreen like in boss fights and later stages. Updates keep adding content. Nobody can stop the dev. Original review: A slightly diff flavor than Boneraiser, but it's $3 and the same ridiculously talented and (I can only assume) good looking dev... Really looking forward to the Campaign mode but worth a shot at least to play around a lil bit till then.

From the erector of Boneraiser minions comes another absolute cog-smacker of a game. Synergies, pathways to combining traits, weapons, drones and items to more powerful forms and highly diverse cast of vessels. This game diverges from BM in that the player is the central damage dealer over their minions (although minions are still a big part of the gameplay loop) and does away with the highly distinct identities of each boneraiser in favour of the aforementioned diverse cast of vessels. For this game I have little if anything to complain about. Its hard but not insanely so*. It gives a very distinct an easy-to-follow pathway for each vessel and mastering their modes of play is incredibly fun and it does well to build tension in each wave with a tension-induced time dilation effect equivalent to running on a treadmill at high speed. *My only critique is one enemy. One. Its run-ender but not in a particularly fun way. The Ethereal watcher. They spawn in multiples, have a hard to predict, hard-to-dodge, borderline hitscan attack that does INSANE damage even at very high health and they almost never spawn alone. Given they only spawn on difficulty 6 but all - and I mean ALL - my runs on that difficulty have hit the wall with a sudden two-tap by this enemy. Please nerf. Other than that, this game is amazing value for what you get. Buy it! 9/10 (nerf the watcher and you'll get a ten)

[u][b]Voids Vigil[/b][/u] is a very generic and average horde survival arena shooter which does nothing exceptional, nor adds anything new to the genre, to make it stand out from its competitors. Moreover, it is basically a clone of [u][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1944570/Boneraiser_Minions/]Boneraiser Minions[/url][/u], the developer's previous game, except that you use weapons instead of letting minions fight for you, it has been reskinned to have a dark and dystopian sci-fi aesthetic, and it has a (slightly) more serious tone but is still chock full of sexual and raunchy innuendos which feel out of place given the setting and tone. Overall, I don't recommend it because it's a simply just a soulless copy of [i]Boneraiser Minions[/i] which recycles most of its content. Additionally, the juvenile potty humor gets stale quickly if you play this right after [i]Boneraiser Minions[/i] and doesn't fit the sci-fi setting and aesthetic nearly as well. Note: this review is current as of Patch v12.6 released on 10 May 2026 and will only be updated for major patches which add significant gameplay changes or achievements. [hr][/hr] [quote][b]S U M M A R Y[/b][/quote] - The gameplay is bog standard for the genre and most runs will feel the same because the majority of the overabundance of classes, weapons, and items are superfluous and don't change how you play the game; - The replay value is very poor, unless you enjoy competing for high scores on the leaderboards, and this is further exemplified if you've previously played [i]Boneraiser Minions[/i] because you'll see most of what the game has to offer within the first few hours or already have seen the recycled content from [i]Boneraiser Minions[/i]; - The graphics are cute and the retro-styled sprites are vivid which really pop against the dark backgrounds and overall aesthetic of the game; - The soundtrack is composed of passable royalty-free dark synthwave songs while the sound effects are good with a proper audio setup; and - The story is almost non-existent and the scant amount that is present feels like a low-effort veneer that was begrudgingly added solely for the purpose of matching the aesthetic. If you're interested, you can find my review of the soundtrack [u][url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561197976187948/recommended/3041990]here[/url][/u]. [hr][/hr] [quote][b]A C H I E V E M E N T S[/b][/quote] The game has 234 achievements which will all be acquired throughout casual play and should take ~45 hours if you play on the easiest difficulty to get the majority of them as quickly as possible. [hr][/hr] [quote][b]R E V I E W[/b][/quote] [h3]Gameplay[/h3] The gameplay is typical for the horde survival genre and introduces nothing new to make the game even remotely unique or exciting. Although discovering things for the first time and learning the mechanics is initially thrilling, this exhilaration quickly wears off after a few hours as you will realistically have seen everything that the game has to offer despite its wide cast of classes, the multitude of weapons, and the plethora of abilities, drones (minions), and passive items, most of which is recycled from [i]Boneraiser Minions[/i] anyways. Although the classes each have slightly different mechanics, the majority of them aren't unique enough to truly give a different experience from one another which ultimately leads to runs feeling the same and only slightly changes how you approach the game from a tactical perspective. The weapons also have a similar issue because there is no discernable difference between them and, thus, they feel superficial rather than impactful. Despite this, there is an interesting system which groups the weapons by, and scales their damage based on, certain elements but the game is easy enough that this system can be completely ignored by casual players; however, taking advantage of it makes the game extremely easy and you can easily delete bosses within a second of spawning into the arena. The only time that you might want to take advantage of this is if you are playing on the hardest difficulty (which still isn't that challenging) or if you are competing for a high score on the leaderboards. The game has five different game modes: - Story, where you go from arena to arena, visit shops in between each, and fight the boss at the end; - Campaign, which is the same as the story mode except there is an open map and you can choose which nodes to visit; - Survival, where you try to stay alive for as long as possible until the enemies outscale you or your computer can no longer run the game; - Boss Rush, which is essentially the story mode but the levels only contain bosses; - Daily/weekly seeded runs, where you can compete in a challenge run for a high score on the leaderboard; and - Card mini-game, which is similar to [i]Triple Triad[/i] from [u][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/39150/FINAL_FANTASY_VIII/]Final Fantasy VIII[/url][/u] but is stripped-down and isn't worth playing at all. [h3]Sound[/h3] The soundtrack is composed of decent royalty-free dark and gritty synthwave songs which match the theme and aesthetic of the game quite well and don't become irritating despite looping quickly; however, they aren't worth listening to outside of the game unless you're really into the genre. The sound effects are good with a proper set of headphones as they are deep and resounding. [h3]Story[/h3] The story is vague and minimalistic, only being presented in cryptic messages shown prior to the title screen and whenever you win a run. The concept has plenty of potential for expansion, especially if it were to lean more into the hacker theme, but I don't think anything else will be done with it despite the fact that the developer has the ability to write eloquently as evidenced by their quippy tutorial dialogue which made me laugh a few times. [h3]Conclusion[/h3] Overall, I don't recommend it because it's simply a very average, run-of-the-mill horde survival game that is a cheap clone of the developer's previous entry, Boneraiser Minions. If you've already played that then you've essentially played this game as there is barely any functional difference between the two and a fair amount of content has been recycled. The best the game can offer is a few hours of fun as you unlock things but the novelty quickly wears off after that.

Also the art style doesn't make it easy to see what the hell is going on. Otherwise it's decent in gameplay, upgrading weapons and drones.. but.. can't recommend the game.

Good garlic-like by the boner minions guys Based around short waves so you're not spending 45+ minutes on a run Builds are quite original for the genre, power-ups are not your standard area/frequency/power modifiers but rather, you have a mix of weapons, elemental attributes, drones, active/passive powers plus your class modifiers. Only thing I'm not too sure is particularly relevant is the plain old points system, which are used for leaderboard purposes. But overall it's been a good time.

Yes, the screen will eventually be covered in enemy bullets. But your character will have a shield, your weapons will have shields, your weapons will shoot shields, your drones will have shields and will be armed with weapons that shoot shields. Superb pixel art and chill bullet hell gameplay starring an eclectic cast of character classes. Great fun in 30-minute increments and many achievements to unlock.

Maybe it's just because Boneraiser Minions really clicked for me (by far my favorite "survivor-like," even more so than Vampire Survivors itself), but the fact that this title feels like it's consciously trying to be different from that one instead of evolving it just kind of rubs me the wrong way. Not a terrible game, and might appeal to those who wanted more of a challenge than Boneraiser offers, but the fact that Boneraiser has continued to get updates even after this came out gives me the impression that the dev themselves realizes that they kind of took a step or two back here. There is quite a lot of content (5 modes with multiple difficulty levels, like 30 characters, 200+ achievements, leaderboards) to be had here for $5 though so go ahead and check the game out for yourself since there's not much to lose.

A significant step down from the previous, similar title from the same developer, Boneraiser Minions. Classes are far more simplistic, there are no currencies to be gained or spent between runs, instead of a class skill tree you just get a couple of modifiers per class and no other changes.

A Survivors/Bullet Hell Roguelike that is visually dark, gritty, and alien. Sprite work is rough but adds to the charm. Diverse with game modes, difficulties options, unlockables, characters, and weapon builds. There is a lot to offer for such a well executed, little game. Well worth the price. Pick this one up when you can. Great on the Steam Deck.

From the same dev as Boneraiser Minions, same DNA, completely different setting tho. Grimy sci-fi aesthetic, robotic hordes, auto-firing weapons orbiting your vessel Brotato-style. Comparing it directly to Boneraiser would be unfair and a bit beside the point. Where Boneraiser is about army composition, here you have more direct control over your damage output through your weapon loadout. The build crafting feels more hands-on and intentional as a result. Maybe it's not the deepest game in the genre, but it doesn't need to be. It's just genuinely good. A solid pick for any fan of the Vampire Survivors sub-genre.
I'd rather play Nova Drift. Also you didn't need to remove a lot of Boneraiser's QOL (like cogs not despawning, and cogs being pulled to you at the end of every sector)

strong follow-up to Boneraiser Minions, even if I would ultimately recommend that title over this one to most +the gameplay feels fluid, fast, & fun, despite the mechanical simplicity +the upgrades shop system is well done with well-balanced risk/reward and diverse viable build paths +several, meaningfully different, game modes +the ability to roll from one game mode into another, with build progression saved, is a smart twist +minimalist scifi aesthetic with surreal touches +tough but fair "challenge" achievements +-a huge variety of classes. Probably too many, in fact, that some fail to truly differentiate themselves. Less is sometimes more -some modes (particularly Campaign) can feel downright unfair until you unlock enough items. Rolling poorly with half of the available shop items as unpurchasable feels incredibly bad -Clashful Cards is still an undercooked, throw-away game mode -the maps themselves could use more variety in terms of shape & hazards -no ability to save and close the game mid-run is horrible for the long 1hr+ Campaign runs

Voids Vigil is an ambitious roguelite action game developed and published by caiysware that successfully blends the addictive progression of survivor-style shooters with the customization depth of an RPG and the strategic planning of an auto-battler. Rather than simply copying popular genre trends, it builds its own identity through a rich collection of ships, weapons, abilities, and upgrades that constantly encourage experimentation. Set within a mysterious region of space corrupted by a phenomenon known as The Void, the game places players in command of powerful robotic vessels tasked with surviving relentless waves of mechanical enemies while uncovering increasingly dangerous challenges. At its core, the gameplay focuses on movement, positioning, and build creation. Weapons fire automatically, allowing players to concentrate on dodging incoming attacks, gathering resources, and choosing upgrades that strengthen their machine. While this approach makes the game easy to pick up, the underlying systems provide surprising complexity. Every run presents choices that can dramatically alter how a build develops, from selecting specialized drones and destructive weaponry to unlocking passive bonuses and unique abilities. The result is a satisfying gameplay loop where every decision matters and no two sessions feel exactly alike. One of the game's strongest qualities is the sheer number of customization options available. Players can experiment with a vast arsenal of weapons that evolve and transform throughout a run. Drones provide additional offensive and defensive support, while elemental affinities and modifiers create powerful synergies that reward creative thinking. A weapon that begins as a simple projectile launcher may eventually become a devastating screen-clearing force when paired with the right upgrades. Discovering these combinations becomes one of the most enjoyable aspects of the experience, giving players a constant incentive to try new strategies. The progression system extends well beyond individual runs. Multiple vessel classes offer distinct starting attributes and playstyles, encouraging repeated playthroughs. Some ships excel at aggressive combat, while others favor survivability or specialized tactics. Unlockable content steadily expands the available options, ensuring that progress feels meaningful even when a run ends in failure. This long-term advancement helps maintain player motivation and creates a strong sense of growth over time. Another highlight is the game's economy and upgrade structure. Throughout each mission, players gather resources that can be spent at various shops offering new equipment, blueprints, abilities, and enhancements. These choices introduce a strategic layer that complements the action. Players must carefully decide whether to improve current strengths or invest in tools that may become valuable later in the run. This balance between immediate survival and long-term planning adds depth that many games in the genre lack. Voids Vigil also delivers an impressive amount of content. Beyond its primary survival-focused gameplay, it includes multiple modes, online leaderboards, procedural events, and varying challenges that help keep the experience fresh. Runs can be tailored to different play sessions, whether players want a quick burst of action or a longer, more demanding challenge. The procedural structure ensures that enemy encounters, rewards, and progression paths remain unpredictable enough to sustain replayability over dozens of hours. Visually, the game adopts a vibrant futuristic aesthetic that suits its robotic theme. Explosions, energy weapons, drones, and swarming enemies fill the screen with colorful effects without completely sacrificing readability. The battlefield can become chaotic during later stages, but the visual design generally allows players to track threats and navigate through dense combat situations. The audio design complements the action with impactful weapon sounds and energetic music that enhance the feeling of commanding an increasingly powerful machine. What ultimately makes Voids Vigil stand out is how successfully it combines accessibility with depth. Newcomers can enjoy its straightforward controls and automatic combat mechanics, while experienced players can dive into the intricate systems governing builds, synergies, and progression. Every run offers opportunities for discovery, experimentation, and optimization, creating the kind of addictive "one more run" appeal that defines the best roguelites. Although the game may not possess the massive production values of larger-budget releases, it compensates with intelligent design, generous content, and a clear understanding of what makes the genre engaging. Its rewarding progression, extensive customization, and excellent replay value make it a compelling choice for fans of action roguelites and survivor-style games alike. Voids Vigil is an impressively crafted indie roguelite that delivers a satisfying blend of fast-paced combat, deep build customization, and long-term progression. With its wealth of unlockables, diverse playstyles, and highly replayable structure, it succeeds as both an accessible entry point for newcomers and a rewarding challenge for genre veterans. Rating: 9/10

Voids Vigil is a significant downgrade compared to it's predecessor, Boneraiser Minions. While it's not a bad game, it feels super lackluster and unimpactful, whereas BM made your choices relevant. Gameplay mostly boils down to WASDing to collect resources and evade attackers and ocasionally picking up upgrades. The problem is, there's never a OH SHI- moment, be in in terms of excitement or desperation. BM kept things interesting through experimentation and meta progression, but VV is more linear in this regard, even if there are plenty of vessels (classes) and items to collect. Again, it's not bad, more like "eh". Wait for a sale if you really want to try it out.

This game is awesome. Has multiple game modes with fun and innovative twists on the survivors formula. High speed twitch bullet hell gaming that requires actual mechanical skill that keeps the gameplay from getting stale and repetitive like a lot of other games in the genre. Lots of characters and a good amount of build and item variety. People that leave this game a negative review are not cool 69 gamer guys; in fact they actually suxors and probably could never place top 10 on the leader boards, even on argon difficulty. 🤡 Buy this if you want to play a survivors style game that requires you to actually stay awake and is more than a mindless dopamine releaser skinner box.
I liked it, lots of systems to tinker with, can start playing instantly. It's a bit hard to see what's actually working, hopefully i'll learn over time.
As usually Caiys making high quality rogue-lites at a very low price, similar to his previous games in terms of features, different modes, different characters, gets more complex as you play.
A nice evolution of the survivor genre that feels mixed with some hardcore shmup from the 80s with stylish sprites in a cybernetic pantheon setting
Fun Bullet Heaven!
Great arena survival game at a great price. GEM!
Great sense of style as usual, and a lot of unlockables. The game moves pretty fast; a lot faster than many other games in the genre. Fun and challenging survivors-like.

If you love Vampire Survivors or Brotato, this game is from the same team that created Boneraiser Minions. Multiple difficulties and classes to unlock. I played 7 hours and just scratched the surface.
Fun brotatemup with great pixel-art, great atmosphere, great aesthetics, & good music. Absolute bargain.
I want to like it. It has plenty of modes and kind of overloads you with play options, I wish it was more focused. Not terrible, but wasn't for me.
If you like Boneraiser Minions, this feels like a darker, more streamlined version with faster runs and more creative weapons.
Another great bullet heaven from Caiys, with lots of content and enough unique about it to differentiate itself from Boneraiser Minions. Highly recommend.
